title: Frozen successor replay of latency-aware taker reversal

frozenPolicy.trigger: first 10-second YES-mid displacement >= 0.02, re-arm inside the 0.02 band
frozenPolicy.executablePrices: YES ask to enter and YES bid to exit; NO uses binary complement
frozenPolicy.depth: at least one visible share at both legs; stale/missing legs censored
frozenPolicy.latencyUsage: same request-start-to-receipt proxy at both legs; order-write latency is unobserved

result.reversal: No signal fired in any of the 1s, 3s, or 10s horizons at p50/p90/p99 latency.
result.conclusion: This fixed 2-cent/10-second strategy was inactive on the measured successor suffix. That is not evidence of a losing trade edge; it is also not profitability evidence. The hypothesis remains untested on this suffix because the strategy generated no candidate trades.

limitations: A 2-cent move trigger produced no observations, so no P&L or uncertainty interval can be estimated.
The file records roughly one public-book record every 12.3 seconds in aggregate across the entire sampled universe, not a per-market high-frequency feed.
One-share top-of-book counterfactuals do not model queue position, market impact, or actual order-write latency.
The explored suffix cannot be reused to tune a lower threshold and then call that result out-of-sample.
